summary.name: Web conferencing
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article describing web conferencing as an umbrella term for webinars, webcasts and web meetings, and tracing its history and features.
use_cases: comparing hosted and on-premises conferencing models
researching history of online meeting software
reviewing standard features of web meeting tools
background on online teaching and virtual conferences
summary.what_it_does: The page explains web conferencing as an umbrella term covering webinars, webcasts and web meetings, made possible by Internet technologies such as TCP/IP. It describes typical features: slideshow presentations, live video, VoIP audio, text chat, polls, whiteboarding, screen and application sharing, file sharing, and meeting recording. It covers deployment models (hosted service, software, and on-premises appliance) and pricing models for vendor-hosted services. It also gives a historical timeline of products such as NetMeeting, PlaceWare, WebEx, GoToMeeting, Adobe Connect and Jitsi, plus the IETF xcon standardization effort.
notable: Describes hosted, software and on-premises appliance deployment models
Covers history from PLATO and IRC to WebEx, GoToMeeting and Jitsi
Notes IETF xcon working group and BFCP (RFC 4582) standardization effort
caveats: Web conferencing technologies are not standardized, which the page says reduces interoperability and increases platform dependence and cost
Vendor-hosted services are usually paid per user-minute, flat fee, or sliding seat-based rate
